title: Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) Protocol for Imaging Living Materials
author: Hans Priks
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bekcjcsw
materials: Increase the thermostat temperature to 37 °C (inlet and outlet of the chamber should be closed at this point). Do not leave the critical point dryer unattended while the temperature is rising as the pressure can exceed the safety limit of the chamber. Control the internal pressure so it does not exceed 110 bar by opening the chamber outlet (should be done slowly as too fast gas release can cool the reactor and turn supercritical state back to liquid state). Adjust the outlet so that the pressure gauge stays stable around 105 bar as the temperature is rising Leave the outlet open as it is, when 37 °C is achieved (do not open the outlet more, as the faster gas release can cool the reactor).

steps.title: Fix Sample
steps.instruction: Fix the sample using a solution of 3.7% volume formaldehyde in 0.1 M phosphate buffer.

substeps.instruction: Submerge sample in fixation solution and incubate at room temperature for 24:00:00.
Replace the fixation solution and incubate at room temperature for another 24:00:00.

steps.title: Dehydrate Sample
steps.instruction: Dehydrate samples at room temperature using an ascending ethanol (EtOH) series in milli-Q water.

substeps.instruction: Submerge sample in each EtOH solution and incubate for a minimum of 02:00:00 per step before changing the solution.
Incubate in 99.5% volume EtOH overnight.
Use 99.5% volume EtOH for storage.

steps.title: Prepare Critical Point Dryer
steps.instruction: Set up the critical point dryer (E3100, Quorum Technologies) for sample processing.

substeps.instruction: Cool the dryer to 15 °C using a thermostat (Proline RP 1845, LAUDA) with an external temperature probe.
Open the dryer, mount the samples, and close the dryer according to producer instructions.

steps.title: Purge Chamber
steps.instruction: Purge the chamber to remove ethanol and introduce CO2.

substeps.instruction: Slightly open the outlet and purge the chamber for 00:05:00 (ensure bubbling in the external EtOH bottle is not too intensive).
Close the outlet first, then the inlet to avoid pressure drop.
Connect the dryer outlet to a half-full bottle of EtOH under a fume hood to capture residues.
Purge the chamber with fresh CO2 6–8 times in 30–60 min intervals: open CO2 inlet, slightly open outlet to purge for 00:05:00, close outlet, then close CO2 inlet.

steps.title: Perform Critical Point Drying
steps.instruction: Process the samples through the supercritical state and depressurize.

substeps.instruction: Allow chamber pressure to drop until it reaches 60 bar.
Open CO2 inlet and fill the chamber with liquid CO2.
Leave the outlet open overnight until the chamber is ready to be opened, adjusting the outlet for slight bubbling to avoid pore formation.

steps.title: Recover Samples
steps.instruction: Safely remove samples from the critical point dryer.

substeps.instruction: Remove the outlet tube from the EtOH bottle under the hood to prevent sucking EtOH into the chamber.
Open the outlet to release remaining pressure within 3-5 min.
Remove samples from the chamber and store in a sealable container (e.g., Eppendorf, glass vial, or Falcon tube).

steps.title: Prepare SEM Stubs
steps.instruction: Prepare aluminum SEM pin stubs for sample mounting.

substeps.instruction: Attach conductive double-sided carbon tabs/tape to the stubs.
Label the stubs with a sharpie marker.

steps.title: Section Samples
steps.instruction: Cut samples using liquid N2 cooling depending on the desired imaging outcome.

substeps.instruction: For artifact-free cross-sections (Fast Incision): Immerse sample with forceps and scalpel in liquid N2 for 00:00:20 and instantly cut with a fast incision (wear protective eyewear).
For colony-material interactions and size/shape (Slow Incision): Immerse sample with forceps and scalpel in liquid N2 for 00:00:10, then cut after 00:00:03 at room temperature with a slow incision.

steps.title: Mount and Coat Samples
steps.instruction: Mount the sectioned samples and apply a conductive coating.

substeps.instruction: Pick up the cut sample with forceps and gently press it onto the two-sided carbon tape.
Coat the sample with a 7.5 nm gold layer using a high vacuum sputter coater (EM ACE600, Leica Microsystems).

steps.title: Image Samples
steps.instruction: Image the gold-coated samples using a tabletop scanning electron microscope (TM3000, Hitachi).

substeps.instruction: Perform imaging under high vacuum and 15 kV accelerating voltage.
